stage: validation of the round-30 text changes, run before the paired head-to-head

arms.PLe_final: compressed + tightened + the new L1 carve-out for continuously displayed state
arms.MSm_old: data_v1/MSm.txt, frozen v1 text, the arm MSc was split out of
arms.MSm_new: v2 draft: construct narrowed to inference, L5's negotiation example replaced

hypotheses.H1_S04: PLe S04 (chemical plant, continuously displayed state) moves off [1,1,1] into its 2|3|4 prereg. This is the one change made to fix a known failure; if it does not move, the L1 carve-out did not bind and should be reverted.
hypotheses.H2_no_collateral: Every other PLe cell that was prereg-consistent at the compression commit stays consistent. The tightening was wording-only and must not move labels.
hypotheses.H3_MSc_flat: MSc stays at or above 71/72 prereg-consistent cells.
hypotheses.H4_double_count: MSm_new drops relative to MSm_old on tasks where the other party's stance is stated outright and needs no inference — N09 (dealer names a floor price) above all, and N08/S05 to a lesser degree if v1's MSm was riding on the negotiation example rather than on the inference.
hypotheses.H5_inference_preserved: MSm_new does NOT drop on tasks whose difficulty really is multi-agent inference: N07 (client's needs are unstated) stays 3+, and N08/S05 stay high, because several parties' beliefs genuinely do interact there. A drop here would mean the narrowing cut construct, not overlap.

decision_rule: H1 fails -> revert the L1 carve-out. H2 or H3 fails -> the wording pass cost something and gets re-examined line by line. H4 fails with H5 holding -> v1's MSm was not in fact double-counting and the narrowing is unjustified. H5 fails -> the narrowing overshot and MSm needs its scope widened again.
